messages.author: cb61691b4e146c12
messages.subject: Error: Hessian is singular....help!
parts:
Hi everyone!

I am trying to create occupancy models using the function occu() and most of them are working, but one of my covariates is giving me some trouble with the "Error:Hessian is singular. Try providing starting values or using fewer covariates."

I tried using the coef() function with some simpler models and then using those values as starting values in the other models, and sometimes it works but some models are still giving me the error.  My data is yellow perch occupancy data, with a bunch of environmental covariates for the sampling sites. The covariate that I think  is causing trouble is "vegetation" which has 20 categorical options. I've read through the other solutions people have given for this problem, but it is still giving me trouble. Help please!

Thanks!
Kaitlyn

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Error: Hessian is singular....help!
parts:
Hi Kaitlyn,

how many sites are in each level of the covariate 'vegetation' (which then is really a factor, right ?) ? Can you do this: table(vegetation) ?
Probably, there are many vegetation types that are represented by very few sites.

What's the typical modeling looking like ? Can you give a summary of a model fit ?

Best regards  --- Marc

Hi Kaitlyn,

I think you can't really have categories of a factor that have a single site. I would cut down the number of categories in the vegetation factor quite drastically, such that each have at least 5-10 sites or so.

Not sure what's wrong with lake level LM. Can you do table(lake) ?

Best regards  ---  Marc
